advice_0: Run canharbor web open in a terminal to open a fresh pairing link. Links expire after 60 seconds and work once. Checking the connection does not redeem the old link.
advice_1: The service denied this request. Check browser access and session status first. If access has expired, run canharbor web open for a fresh pairing link. Pairing links work once; this error can also indicate an access or request-verification failure.
advice_2: Control has expired. Refresh status, then explicitly acquire control and start the channel if needed. Nothing is resumed automatically.
advice_3: Another session or client holds this resource. Refresh status and review the owner before explicitly acquiring control. Do not repeat the operation until the resource is available.
advice_4: Refresh session status. Review the selected session and current configuration before explicitly applying changes again. For recordings, an existing request identifier may refer to different settings.
advice_5: Refresh the list: this resource may have expired or been removed. A missing submission or run result does not prove that execution never occurred.
advice_6: The service reached a resource limit. Review active recordings, sessions and tests, then explicitly stop unneeded work before trying again.
advice_7: Check that the local service is running, then check the connection. A failed response can leave an operation's outcome unknown. Review session status and submission history before repeating an operation.
advice_8: Review the current resource and submission history. Reconnect explicitly if disconnected; sending and control are never restored automatically.
validation: Review the {{subject}}. The service message identifies the rejected value; correct it before submitting again.
recordingSubject: recording name, duration and source session
stressSubject: test plan, selected channels and resource limits
